title: User deactivation events via transactional outbox
name: User deactivation relay

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code keeps the identity database and the downstream session service consistent? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does DeactivateUser insert the outbox row in the same transaction as the user update?
choices: So the broker receives the event before the database commits
So the event can be published by the request handler without a relay
So the status change and the record of the event to publish commit or roll back together, avoiding a dual write
To make the UPDATE hold its row lock for longer

questions.prompt: What happens when DeactivateUser is called for a user who is already deactivated?
choices: It returns ErrNotActive and nothing is written, because the UPDATE matches no row and no event is inserted
A second event is added to the outbox and the sessions are revoked again
It returns nil after updating deactivated_at again
The transaction fails with a unique constraint violation on the outbox

questions.prompt: The session service receives the same deactivation message twice. What does SessionRevoker.Handle do the second time?
choices: Deletes the user's sessions again, which is harmless but also deletes sessions created after the first run
Rolls back because of the primary key conflict
Returns an error so the broker redelivers the message
Inserts nothing into processed_events, sees zero rows affected, and commits without touching sessions
